facts.statement: The type species of the genus Kendrickichthys is Kendrickichthys cavernosus, described by Dennis and Miles in 1980.
Kendrickichthys was an extinct arthrodire placoderm that lived during the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
facts.quote: Kendrickichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Kendrickichthys have been found in the Gogo Formation in the Kimberley region of Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Gogo Formation of the Kimberley region of Australia.

facts.statement: Researchers believed Kendrickichthys was durophagous, meaning it preyed on hard-shelled creatures like mollusks.
facts.quote: It was thought to be durophagous, meaning that it preyed upon hard-shelled creatures such as mollusks.

facts.statement: Kendrickichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Kendrickichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which belongs to the clade Pachyosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The parent group of Kendrickichthys is the family Mylostomatidae.
Kendrickichthys lived from 382.31 to 372.15 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)
